observation.visible_scene: A wide, calm expanse of blue water occupies the lower half of the frame beneath a pale blue sky. A low, forested shoreline stretches horizontally across the middle distance, with a thin haze band along the left horizon. A single bright cumulus cloud sits in the upper-right sky, mirrored by a soft white reflection on the water directly below it. The foreground water shows fine, parallel ripples.
visible_changes: The water surface ripples continuously: the foreground wave pattern shifts and reforms from frame to frame throughout the excerpt.
The white reflection of the right-side cloud on the water shimmers and slightly deforms/undulates across the sequence.
The sky cloud, the thin left cloud band, and the distant shoreline keep fixed positions relative to the frame edges, so there is no evident camera pan, tilt, or zoom.
No separate object enters, exits, or translates across the scene; the only visible motion is the water's surface texture and its reflection.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause of the ripples (wind or current) and what preceded them before t=0.000.
Any camera movement or change in the scene before the start or after the end of this cropped segment.
uncertain_details: A very slight camera sway cannot be entirely excluded, but the background landmarks appear stationary.
The ripple phase at the two crop boundaries is arbitrary; the surface motion is already ongoing and continues beyond the excerpt, not an onset or completion.

and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
